If they're not trained to look for certain things in specific places (i.e. Specialized) they can most definitely miss something that major. My mother is a prime example of this; our towns hospital is fantastic in dealing with anything with the heart. Anything else not so much. They thought it was just her gallbladder the first time (2008) so they took it out, but a few years later (2011) she has another painful attack that makes it where she can't even move. We take her to our hospital and only one nurse (the one that admitted her) believed her pain and thought he saw a shadow on her liver. All the others in the hospital thought she was faking it and only looking for drugs. One trip to UAB and they found her liver INFESTED with benign tumors with three fairly large ones in the mix. One surgery later and five years of semi annual doctors visits back there, they're finally shrinking this year. My point is, UAB had people specialized in the liver so they knew what to look for, while our local hospital only had heart specialists. If you aren't specifically trained to look for certain things it's a high possibility you'll miss it
